**Urinvejsblødning** (urinary tract bleeding) is a clinical condition that serves as a critical component in the evaluation of patient safety within the Danish healthcare system. It is formally defined as one of the four specific types of severe bleeding—alongside intracranial, gastrointestinal, and pulmonary bleeding—that constitute the outcome variable for Indicator 7 [^src1]. 

Indicator 7 is a national quality indicator designed to measure the incidence of severe bleeding among patients with pre-existing atrial fibrillation [^src1]. Because anticoagulation therapy carries inherent hemorrhagic risks, tracking *urinvejsblødning* and the other three major bleeding types allows health authorities to monitor treatment safety and quality across national, regional, and local health clusters [^src1]. The framework for identifying these severe bleeding events is tied to internationally recognized criteria from the ISTH and relies on registry data from the Danish National Patient Register (Landspatientregistret) [^src1]. 

Beyond its explicit inclusion in this definitional framework for Indicator 7, the available documentation does not provide further statistical, chronological, or clinical details specific to *urinvejsblødning* as an isolated entity.
